why_trail.why: Reproduced the handoff's narrowing myself: demo script gave 12/12 assertions OK. An engine refusal through the door moves refusals and reaches episode_capture.mechanical_fields(); the door's own rejection (missing condition_id on spine_evidence attest) moved refusals 0 and left mcp_calls.jsonl unchanged. Confirms target is exactly the door's own _tool_error(...) short-circuit path.

Implemented door-own rejection capture inside scripts/mcp_spine_server.py. Because call_tool()'s existing choke-point pin (tests/test_mcp_identity.py::IdentityBindingPinTests) restricts every return in that function to literally as_result(run_engine(...)) or _tool_error(...), I first tried a separate _reject() wrapper and it broke that pin (14 offenders) -- so I folded the logging into _tool_error itself via optional tool=/rejection_class= kwargs instead of adding a new call shape, which keeps the pin's AST check satisfied while giving every in-scope rejection its own JSONL record. REJECTIONLOG defaults beside the spine (SPINE_REJECTION_LOG env override), one record per call to _log_rejection with a write-failure path that writes a fresh stderr line on every occurrence, never batched. python -m pytest -q tests/test_mcp_friction_capture.py tests/test_mcp_spine_server.py tests/test_mcp_identity.py tests/test_mcp_imperative_equivalence.py -> 55 passed. Full suite: 2282 passed, 1 skipped, 1 failed (map/INDEX.md staleness, expected and deferred to the guards step). git diff against scripts/checklist_engine.py is empty. Demo script still 12/12.

Launched the real server as a subprocess against a throwaway spine and induced 3 real door-own rejections (unknown-action, missing-required-argument, unknown-tool) via .agent-work/epic-418-followon/commander-f2/evidence/g2-friction-capture/seed_rejections.py, landing mcp_rejections.jsonl beside it. Built an episode delta whose mechanical.run='epic-418-followon/commander-f2' (matching this run's own nested work-id) and whose artifact-ref cites the JSONL, the seeding script and the two source deliverables. Applied with 'python scripts/apply_episode_delta.py --delta .../episode-delta.json --store-root episodes' -> created episode:epic-418-followon_commander-f2-001. Read the written file back at episodes/active/epic-418-followon_commander-f2-001.md. Verified with 'python scripts/verify_episode_captured.py epic-418-followon/commander-f2 --store-root episodes' -> exit 0, '1 episode(s) recorded'.

python -m pytest -q -> 2283 passed, 1 skipped (full suite, green). tests/test_retirement_guard.py -> 16 passed. Rebuilt the code map (python -m scripts.code_map build --root .); map/INDEX.md diffed 3 lines (entity count); tests/test_code_map.py::MapTreeFreshnessTests -> 2 passed. Re-ran the demo script -> 12/12 OK, unchanged. git check-ignore on every committed deliverable (mcp_spine_server.py, test_mcp_friction_capture.py, the new episode, the evidence scripts/JSONL/delta, map/INDEX.md, my own plan file) -> exit 1 for all (not ignored). Found and flagged tc1: episode_capture.manifest_root()'s doubled-path defect (documented for 2-segment work-ids in tests/test_work_id_nesting.py) reappears one level deeper for my own 3-segment implementer-plan work-id, writing a stray untracked .agent-work/epic-418-followon/epic-418-followon/... tree; deleted (untracked, harmless) rather than fixed since episode_capture.py is outside this run's ownership.
